title: What Neurodivergent Adults Need When Knowing Isn’t Enough: A Neurodiversity-Affirming Guid
description: Some days you can lead a meeting and still get dinner on the table. Other days, answering one text feels impossible. Most advice is written for the first kind of day. This book is written for the second. If you’re a neurodivergent adult with ADHD, autism, or AuDHD, you may know the rest of the pattern. You hold it together all day, then fall apart the minute you get home. Your executive function runs dry by mid-afternoon. Sensory overload builds before you notice it, and masking leaves you with nothing left for the people you love. When burnout hits, rent, work, and family still need you, so stopping to recover isn’t an option. You’ve tried harder. You’ve tried new systems. What you need is help that still works when energy, money, and support run low. What Neurodivergent Adults Need When Knowing Isn’t Enough is a practical, neurodiversity-affirming guide grounded in current research. It helps you decide what to change first and fit each strategy to the capacity you actually have. Inside, you’ll discover how to: Find your survival speed for everyday essentials, so meals, laundry, and bills still happen on your worst days Catch overload early with a personal warning system that flags trouble before a shutdown or meltdown Ask for what you need at work and at home, with short scripts you can say in under a minute Lower the cost of masking through small, reversible experiments in the places where it feels safe Recover from burnout while life keeps going , and restart a routine that slipped without starting from zero Worried it’s another book you’ll start and never finish? Every chapter stands on its own, opens with a two-minute summary, and includes at least one free option. title: Neurodivergent Adults: Thriving with ADHD, Autism, and More in a Neurotypical World
description: You're not broken. You're neurodivergent—and you're not alone. More adults than ever are discovering they have ADHD, autism, dyslexia, OCD, and other forms of neurodivergence—often after years of feeling “off,” misunderstood, or exhausted from trying to fit in. Neurodivergent Adults: Thriving with ADHD, Autism, and More in a Neurotypical World is a practical, compassionate guide to understanding your brain, breaking free from shame, and building a life that truly works for you . Written by psychotherapist and fellow neurodivergent Richard L. Travis, this book is packed with real-life examples, helpful tools, unmasking strategies, and empowering resources. Whether you're newly diagnosed, self-identifying, or supporting a loved one, you’ll find insights that resonate deeply—and help you move from merely surviving to genuinely thriving. Inside you'll discover: Why so many adults are diagnosed late (especially women, LGBTQ+, and BIPOC individuals) How to manage executive dysfunction, sensory overload, and burnout Relationship tips, communication scripts, and conflict resolution tools Career advice—from accommodations to entrepreneurship Real stories from clients and everyday neurodivergent adults Extensive resources: TED Talks, YouTube channels, podcasts, and worksheets If you’ve ever felt like you’re “too much,” “not enough,” or simply different—this book is for you. Your brain isn’t the problem. The world wasn’t built for it. Let’s change that—together. description: Finally—A Real-World Guide for Autistic Adults Ready to Thrive, Not Mask. Are you an adult who's always felt "different," yet didn’t quite know why? What if neurodivesity isn't a flaw — but an extraordinary way of experiencing the world? The Neurodivergent Path is your empowering roadmap to thriving as an autistic adult, not by "fixing" yourself, but by finally understanding and honoring who you truly are. Inside, you'll discover how to: Embrace your neurodivergent identity and unlearn years of masking or self-doubt Decode sensory processing and create personalized comfort strategies for home and work Master executive function with adaptive systems tailored to how your brain operates Build genuine connections from friendships to romance — on your own terms Navigate the workplace with confidence, communication tools, and self-advocacy skills Manage co-occurring challenges like anxiety, ADHD, and burnout with compassion Cultivate sustainable self-care that nourishes your energy, focus, and emotional resilience This isn't a clinical manual — it's a guide for autistic adults balancing sensory needs, relationships, careers, and self-acceptance. Whether you're newly diagnosed, self-identified, or supporting a neurodivergent loved one, this book offers a pathway to understanding and peace. Written with warmth, clarity, and lived insight, this guide helps you navigate adult life on the autism spectrum — from managing sensory overload and executive function challenges to building authentic relationships, advocating for your needs, and finding calm in a neurotypical world. description: AUDIBLE EDITOR'S PICK The bestselling, paradigm-shifting study of neurodivergent women—those with ADHD, autism, synesthesia, high sensitivity, and sensory processing disorder—exploring why these traits are overlooked in women and how society benefits from allowing their unique strengths to flourish . As a successful Harvard and Berkeley-educated writer, entrepreneur, and devoted mother, Jenara Nerenberg was shocked to discover that her “symptoms”--only ever labeled as anxiety-- were considered autistic and ADHD. Being a journalist, she dove into the research and uncovered neurodiversity—a framework that moves away from pathologizing “abnormal” versus “normal” brains and instead recognizes the vast diversity of our mental makeups. When it comes to women, sensory processing differences are often overlooked, masked, or mistaken for something else entirely. Nerenberg explores these topics in depth, delving into: Flawed systems that focus on diagnosing younger, male populations. How people assigned female at birth are conditioned to blend in and conform to gender expectations, and how women often don’t learn about their neurological differences until they are adults, if at all. The impact of millions living with undiagnosed or misdiagnosed neurodivergences, and how the misidentification leads to depression, anxiety, low self-esteem, and shame. Practical solutions for neurodivergent people to thrive, not just survive. description: Are meltdowns, shutdowns, and burnout taking more from you than anyone can see? Does Any of This Sound Familiar? You don't notice you're overloaded until it's already too late. Words disappear right when someone demands an answer. You've been masking for so long that ordinary days drain you. Tasks you once did easily now feel impossible to start. A small request can bring up a panic that feels much older. I get it. Whether you're autistic, ADHD, AuDHD, or living with complex PTSD, you keep going through the noise, answer before you're ready, and push on after your energy is gone. You've been told to take deep breaths, listen to your body, or just rest. I know how lonely it feels when the advice was never built for your brain. Breathing drills and body scans can make overwhelm worse. "Listen to your body" fails when your signals are faint or arrive late. Polyvagal books often bury you in jargon and leave you with little you can use. These somatic exercises start from what you can actually manage today, even on a burnout day. But First, a Warning If you want a book that promises to "reset your vagus nerve" in 10 minutes, this isn't it. Every page is optional, and none asks you to relive trauma or force a sensation. What it asks is honesty about your needs. description: From a social emotional learning expert: a book providing simple, science-based, practical advice including scripts, tips and strategies to help Neurodivergent adults who have ADHD, autism or anxiety find the belonging and support of lifelong friendships they seek. Friendship can be hard for many Neurodivergent adults. There is an assumption that good, worthwhile friendships “should” come easy. However, for Neurodivergent adults, there are brain-based reasons why friendship can feel less intuitive. From differences in the parts of the brain that are vital to managing the logistics of a fulfilling social life to difficulty with self-regulation, the way neurodiverse individuals experience social bonding and connection can feel unintuitive. Friendship Skills For Neurodivergent Adults is a guide to navigate these differences, broken into three parts: 1. How friendship works 2. How to find your people 3. title: The Neurodivergent Mind Workbook for Late-Diagnosed Adults : Practical DBT, ACT & CBT Skil
description: Why does life feel so exhausting... even when you've spent your whole life trying to keep up? Do you feel like you're working twice as hard as everyone around you just to make it through the day? Do you rehearse conversations, mask your reactions, and wonder why everyday tasks take so much out of you? Have you been called “lazy,” “too much,” “oversensitive,” or “impossible to please” so often that those words became how you saw yourself? No matter the answer, none of it meant something was wrong with you . You were just living by instructions that were never written for you. In The Neurodivergent Mind Workbook for Late-Diagnosed Adults , Rita Hayes offers a gentle, practical roadmap for understanding yourself, unmasking safely, and building a life shaped around who you are. It draws on proven CBT, ACT, and DBT skills, with no clinical jargon or pressure to "fix" anything. In this book, you will discover: ● The most common myths about neurodivergence , and the science-backed truths that finally dismantle the shame you've internalized for years ● How to navigate the emotional aftermath of a late diagnosis : the relief, grief, anger, and identity shift that often arrive all at once ● A practical toolkit of CBT, ACT, and DBT exercises you can use in real time to regulate emotions and interrupt spirals ● How to recognize your own masking patterns , and unmask without losing your sense of safety ● The truth about why rejection cuts so deep , why emotions can feel hard to find, and what your nervous system actually needs when it tips into a meltdown or shutdown ● Why "if I did it before, why can't I do it now?" is the wrong question , and what to ask yourself instead ● How to break the executive-dysfunction-to-burnout cycle before it takes you down ● What long-term integration

title: Somatic Therapy for Neurodivergent Adults: How to Calm Sensory Overload and Regulate Your
description: Somatic therapy should not leave you feeling more overwhelmed than when you started. For many neurodivergent adults, that is exactly what happens. You sit down to do the exercise. You try to notice your body and slow your breathing. Instead of feeling calmer, you feel irritated, flooded, blank, restless, or more aware of sensations you cannot make sense of. After a while, it starts to feel like the problem must be you. The real explanation has nothing to do with effort. Somatic Therapy for Neurodivergent Adults is a practical guide for ADHD, autistic, and AuDHD adults who want nervous system support that fits the way their unique mind works. This book helps you understand: Why so many standard somatic techniques miss the mark How to tell the difference between overload, shutdown, anxiety, freeze, executive dysfunction, and masking exhaustion Which regulation tools are more likely to help in each state. And tons more! Inside, you’ll learn how to use movement, rhythm, pressure, temperature, visual anchors, structured breathwork, and other low-demand tools that work in everyday life, including at work, in social settings, and during moments when your brain is too overloaded for complicated instructions. This book is designed to be easy to use when focus is low or your nervous system is already strained. Each chapter includes: • chapter takeaways for quick refreshers • diagrams that make the information easier to understand • exercises to help you apply what you just learned You’ll also get 3 exclusive digital bonuses with instant access: • A full-color diagrams PDF with all the book’s diagrams in one place for quick visual review • A Sensory Environment Audit to help you spot the hidden stressors making your nervous system work harder • A Neurodivergent Nervous System Quic
